source.title: Emergence of invariance and disentangling in deep representations

record.tranche_reason: The study trains networks on random labels and reports how fitting changes with an information regularizer; it does not reproduce the unregularized original setup.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for standard CNNs fitting random labels; that cited result is not extracted as a row. The study's own random-label experiment varies the information regularizer β and reports a phase transition. The figure does not give recoverable per-model numeric values.
record.test_reason: The study measures random-label training error using SGD and an information-regularized loss. Its own results bear on V1 in this modified training setting, although they do not establish the unchanged-training-recipe clause.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct: random-label memorization requires information in the weights, and their information-regularized loss produces an architecture-robust transition between fitting and underfitting. More precisely, Figure 2 places transitions before β=1, with ResNet close to 1; Figure 1 shows transitions near 1 across dataset sizes.
record.recipe_differences: The random-label experiment uses an explicit information-bottleneck regularizer and sweeps β; it is not the unregularized original training recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with β: the networks overfit below the transition and underfit above it. The text says ResNet transitions close to β=1.

fits_no_version.finding: At β=0.1 with 30,000 examples, information in Small AlexNet's weights increases with label corruption; fully random labels require about 3 additional nats per sample.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorizing increasingly corrupted labels requires increasing information in the weights.

record.problems: The reported per-model error values are only in a figure and cannot be recovered numerically from the supplied text. The experiment changes the loss with an information regularizer, so it does not establish the standard unregularized claim. No uncertainty estimates or random-label comparison to test error are reported in this experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results. The cited Zhang et al. random-label result is prior work, not this study's own result.

untested.parts: Fitting with the original standard loss and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters relative to true-label training. The experiments introduce stochastic weights and an information regularizer.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.
The joint trajectory of perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error across corruption fractions, including preservation of remaining signal.

The effects of weight decay, ordinary dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing them. The information regularizer is a different intervention.
Whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels over training.

missing.what: The study's own Small AlexNet experiment varies dataset size and β and reports high random-label training accuracy below the transition alongside chance-level test performance. Figure 1 is an additional experiment, despite its architecture being adapted from Zhang et al.; it is not merely a cited result.

record.verdict_notes: No precise per-model error values can be recovered from the supplied text. The theoretical prediction of no memorization for β>1 should not substitute for measured high-β error values. This study is neither listed original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the unregularized standard training setup or compare training hyperparameters with true-label training. Its own experiment adds an information regularizer and sweeps β.
Training time relative to true labels and convergence speed across corruption levels are not reported.
Shuffled pixels and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.
The study measures information in weights across corruption levels, not training and test error across those levels.
Weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation are not tested for their effect on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
The study does not compare learning over time for real versus random labels.

rows.subject: Small AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with completely random labels while sweeping the information-regularizer parameter β.
rows.value: Figure 2 shows a phase transition from complete overfitting to underfitting before β=1; no recoverable numeric value.
rows.note: The text says the phase transition appears across the tested architectures. The random-label training setup uses the information regularizer, so this does not establish fitting under the unmodified standard setup.
rows.check: The row combines distinct conditions: complete fitting at low β and underfitting above the transition. Split these into observed and absent/incomplete-fitting conditions; exact high-β errors are unreadable. Figure 2 explicitly reports complete overfitting, so the evidence is not figure-only. The multi-architecture experiment uses learning rate 0.05.

source_check.correct: Split by β regime: complete fitting below the transition has state observed; above the transition, the model underfits. Exact higher-β errors are not stated.
source_check.problem: A single partial state merges complete fitting and underfitting under different regularization strengths.
